original_gates.evidence: Foreground woman points toward working/store area; the separate man faces her and supports a plan; grain work and store appear together. This supports directed interaction, not actual authority or compliance.

Raked grain, loaded carts, store ramp and sacks inside are clear. The uninterrupted route from worked grain through the yard boundary to the loaded cart/store is not jointly visible; rear walls/straw/figures obscure the transfer path.

Plan and scene share a circular floor, rear store/ramp and a drainage form. Water emerges into the foreground gutter, but a complete dry-paving-to-inlet-to-outlet-to-lower-wet-ground connection cannot be traced across the retaining wall.

The central face is large enough for qualitative comparison; short dark bob, separated bangs, dark eyes and rounded face are consistent with the appearance reference. No identity or exact biometric match is asserted.
An inhabited agricultural estate inspection reads through the direction gesture, plan, workers, grain yard, loaded carts and storage, rather than costume alone.

selected_source_gate.evidence: Village/field edge, hall, store and multiple loaded carts are present. A single continuous village/field-to-store route is interrupted by foreground figures and middle buildings; all carts cannot be confirmed on that same complete visible route.

limits: A single unpaired image does not establish causal improvement from the new dataset or historical accuracy.
